text:
alex: Heads up — perf regression on the 1F1B experiments after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. PP bubble grew ~40% on 16GB A100 trains when running 4 microbatches. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

marta: saw it on a few trace runs, yep. The new selector picks a different fused attention kernel for seq=1024 which looks fine in isolation but latency across the prep/allreduce phases spikes.

kyle: attaching the quick perf dump I ran this morning. main difference is the allreduce tail and interleaved warmup stalls.

kyle: ```
# snapshot from perf-profiler 
phase: forward
kernel: fused_attn_v2 (chosen)
forward_token_ms: 23.4
allreduce_wait_ms: 11.8
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.87
microbatch: 4
1f1b_window: enabled

previous (fused_attn_v1): allreduce_wait_ms: 6.2
```

devon: hmm kv_cache_hit_ratio 0.87 seems okay. But the allreduce_wait jump is suspect. Could be that the new kernel has a longer compute tail so comm/compute overlap shrinks.

sophie: also noticed more KV cache evictions on long seq customers when microbatch=4. That could force extra mem ops right before allreduce and amplify the tail.

marta: can we repro with microbatch=2 vs 4 and with the old selector? quick A/B will show if it's selector->overlap or just kvcache churn.

alex: good plan. I kicked off two runs: 2480000010 (selector=v2, microbatch=4) and 2480000020 (selector=v1, microbatch=4) and a third 2480000030 (selector=v2, microbatch=2). Will paste results as they come.

rendezvous-bot: [2480000010] run-complete: throughput=820 req/s, avg-pp-latency=184ms, allreduce-avg=12.1ms, comm-compute-overlap=0.63

rendezvous-bot: [2480000020] run-complete: throughput=1030 req/s, avg-pp-latency=130ms, allreduce-avg=6.4ms, comm-compute-overlap=0.82

rendezvous-bot: [2480000030] run-complete: throughput=950 req/s, avg-pp-latency=150ms, allreduce-avg=9.5ms, comm-compute-overlap=0.74

kyle: clear signal — selector=v2 reduces overlap. microbatch=2 recovers some overlap but throughput drops. So it's a tradeoff 

devon: what's the kernel change? I remember v2 switches to a tiled matmul layout that improves locality but may have a longer epilogue. Could increase tail as you say.

marta: yep, the patch is in runtime/kernel-selector: switch to fused_attn_v2 when seq>512 and batch_per_gpu>=16. It used heuristics based on single-GPU microbenchmarks. Multi-GPU interplay not tested.

alex: options: revert selector change, update selector heuristics to include comm/compute overlap estimate, or add a short warmup pre-allreduce (a tiny dummy forward) to prime KV cache and let compute pipelines overlap. Thoughts? :thinking:

sophie: warmup trick could be low-risk. A single `priming_batch=1` that touches KV cache keys might reduce evictions. But if selector is fundamentally longer tail it's only partial.

kyle: can we estimate overlap impact from kernel tail time? If kernel tail adds X ms per microbatch, allreduce overlap reduces by X / (kernel_time + comm_time) roughly. We can simulate with the profiler.

alex: ran a synthetic with artificially appended 6ms tail to fused_attn_v1 and overlap fell to ~0.65 matching v2 numbers. So seems consistent.

devon: patch plan: 1) revert selector in canary for the dedicated pool for 24h, 2) implement an overlap-aware heuristic that penalizes kernels with long epilogues on multi-gpu configs, 3) try priming microbatch in parallel branch.

marta: I'll own (2). Steps: add sampling in selector where we estimate kernel_epilogue_ms from microbench + model seq distribution, then compute expected overlap; fall back to v1 when overlap predicted < 0.75 for 1F1B.

marta: rough pseudo: ```
score = kernel_throughput - penalty*(epilogue_ms / (epilogue_ms + estimated_allreduce))
choose kernel with max score
```

kyle: nice. (3) I can test priming in a feature branch — will run priming=1,2 for microbatch=4 and measure kvcache eviction counters.

sophie: tagging infra to keep an eye on mem pressure: @mike-infra we might see slight mem spike from priming.

mike-infra: noted — will watch. set retention to 10m for the canary so we have quick rollback if OOM.

alex: timeline: revert canary now, selector heuristic PR by EOD (marta), priming branch results tomorrow (kyle). If heuristic looks good, we'll roll to staging and re-evaluate throughput/latency.

devon: add an eval test that runs long-seq customer prompt + 1F1B across kernel variants so we don't regress again silently.

marta: will add to runtime/eval/regressions. Also logging: expose epilogue_ms and chosen_kernel in pp-trace logs for easier postmortems.

alex: thanks all. Good catch. We'll reconvene after the runs. :thumbsup:
